extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NRSA fellowship applicants (F30, F31, F32) to NIAID/NIH
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting NIAID/NIH NRSA individual fellowship (F30, F31, F32) applications, including eligibility, application components, research plan expectations, and post-award obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/Residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must be U.S. citizens, noncitizen nationals, or permanent residents with a valid Permanent Resident Card (Form I-551) at the time of award. People on temporary or student visas are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is determined at award time; temporary/student visa holders cannot receive NRSA individual fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship activity-specific applicant profiles (F30, F31, F32)
rubrics_metrics.description: F30: enrolled in a formally combined clinical and research doctoral program (M.D.-Ph.D., D.V.M.-Ph.D., etc.) and supervised by a sponsor for the research doctoral component. F31: at dissertation research stage, enrolled in Ph.D. or equivalent research degree program or combined professional/clinical and research doctoral program. F32: has a doctoral degree from an accredited institution; may request foreign training with detailed justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the specific activity code (F30, F31, F32) to your training stage and program enrollment; F32 foreign training requires justification explaining why domestic training is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration and non-renewability
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are awarded for a maximum number of years: F30 — 6 years; F31 — 3 years (for NIAID); F32 — 3 years. Fellowships are not renewable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan research timeline and Specific Aims to fit within the maximum, since renewals are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time effort requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships require full-time effort, 12 person months a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to full-time training, fellows may spend on average an additional 25 percent of their time (e.g., 10 hours a week) in part-time research, teaching, or clinical employment, provided those activities do not interfere with, or lengthen, the duration of NRSA training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral payback obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral fellows must repay the government for their grant support. During the first year of your appointment, you'll owe 1 month of payback for every month you're supported by NIH funds. After the first year, you can start paying back. For every month you continue to work—even with funding—you pay back 1 month of your debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your training lasts 2 years, your obligation will be paid in full. If project funding ends after the first year, you can complete payback through at least half-time research or teaching (20 hours/week) and must complete payback within 2 years after termination unless serious extenuating circumstances exist. Failure to repay within 2 years results in owing the full amount plus interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses multiple due dates for fellowship applications: F30, F31 and F32 (non-AIDS)—April 8, August 8, and December 8. AIDS and AIDS-related fellowship applications follow standard AIDS due dates: May 7, September 7, and January 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm deadlines relevant to your FOA and plan reference letter and institutional approvals accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission and following FOA/SF424 instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your application electronically using ASSIST or another NIH submission option. Follow the instructions in the relevant notice of funding opportunity and the supplemental instructions for individual fellowship applications in the SF 424 Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with your business office for the institution's submission approach and consult the Fellowship Grants SOP for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID iD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have an ORCID iD and associate it with their eRA Commons Personal Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow eRA Commons instructions on creating and linking an ORCID iD before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters: number and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Request at least three (but no more than five) reference letters. They must be submitted by your application's due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure letter writers can meet the deadline; review Reference Letter Instructions in the SF 424 Application Guide for what to provide to letter writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: You must comply with NIH public access policy, which includes citing papers from NIH-funded research in your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Public Access of Publications SOP for details; include appropriate citations and PMCID/DOI where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to address rigor and reproducibility. Check the requirements at Guidance: Rigor and Reproducibility in Grant Applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH guidance on experimental design, bias reduction, authentication of key biological resources, and other R&R elements applicable to your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable post-submission materials (fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may send certain materials after submission and before initial peer review. For fellowships, this includes a one-page summary to update your sponsor's funding information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send no more than one page to your scientific review officer at least 30 days before the review meeting; include a note from your business office stating its concurrence or have your authorized organizational representative send the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review purpose and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating your application, reviewers gauge the likelihood the fellowship will enhance your potential for and commitment to a productive research career. For postdocs, they also assess whether you have what it takes to be an independent researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship applications are assigned to CSR review groups based on scientific content and clustered by activity code; understand clustering and streamlining processes that affect discussion time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan overall communication goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Research Plan must communicate clarity, completeness, and coherence; originality, significance, and practicality of goals; a clear description of the research skills and knowledge you want to acquire, and your plan's potential for meeting these objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how training will build skills and contribute to career progression (foundation for predoc; independence for postdoc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects, animals, and ethical training plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plans to include a heterogeneous human subjects population including women and minorities (if applicable), plans to include animals as test subjects (if applicable), and plans to obtain training in ethical research conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address inclusion and animal welfare policies explicitly; include a plan for instruction in responsible research conduct — omission renders the application incomplete and it will not be reviewed until an acceptable plan is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven Specific Aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding the research, start with a hypothesis, then develop Specific Aims and experiments to test it. Be careful not to propose too much since you'll have limited time to accomplish your aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design aims that are feasible within the award duration and commensurate with your experience level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match plan sophistication to applicant level
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers have different expectations for predoctoral candidates than for postdocs and will look at whether the plan fits the applicant's level of research experience. Predocs with little or no experience are not expected to have as sophisticated a plan as postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure research complexity, independence expectations, and training components are appropriate for your stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor review and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask your sponsor to review your Research Plan for thoroughness, consistency, and effective presentation. Read what your sponsor and co-sponsor write so information provided by you and them works well together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies between applicant and mentor statements hurt review; reviewers resent evidence the mentor didn't read the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement and biosketch content
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Personal Statement section describe your level of research experience, passion for research, strengths, and weaknesses, and how you plan to bolster weaknesses. Highlight publications (especially for F31) and state what you hope to gain from a fellowship as opposed to conducting research under your mentor's grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid about experience and explicit about professional development plans that the fellowship will enable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for reviewers to read your application by writing a well-organized one. Use headers, charts, graphs, and other elements that will make your application appealing and user friendly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good organization reduces reviewer burden and helps avoid negative impact from avoidable omissions or confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predoctoral Research Plan emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral Research Plan should present a thorough grounding in the design, methodology, and analysis of a research protocol; research stages (proposal, execution, presentation, publication); problem solving; and opportunities to interact with other members of the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with at least 1–2 years of lab experience tend to perform better in review because they can write a state-of-the-art Research Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral career-development expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: As a postdoctoral fellow, you should be taking steps now to become an independent investigator (e.g., publishing papers and applying for grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate a trajectory toward independence and include milestones (publications, grant applications) in your timeline and training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy required components (F30/F31/F32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Strategy must include: a well-defined research project (typically hypothesis-driven); background leading to and significance of the proposed research; research approach (design and methods) for achieving the Specific Aims, the rationale for the proposed approach, potential pitfalls, and expected/alternative outcomes of the proposed studies; a resource sharing plan; and a plan for the responsible conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are explicitly required; omission (especially of the RCR plan) can make the application incomplete and delay review.

rubrics_metrics.name: F30 educational information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: F30 application must include educational information, e.g., description of the dual-degree program in which applicant is enrolled, and the research training plan should facilitate the fellow’s transition to a residency program or to a postdoctoral program as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed training fits within the dual-degree program and furthers clinical/residency or postdoctoral objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: F31/F32 training-plan specificity and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The research training plan (F31/F32) should be individually tailored and well-integrated with the applicant's research project. It should describe the skills and techniques to be learned, any planned non-research activities (e.g., professional development), and provide a timeline for proposed training and related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete training activities, milestones, and a timeline that demonstrate feasibility and alignment with career goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipends, tuition, institutional allowances, and childcare
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships pay stipends, tuition and fees, and institutional allowances for training-related expenses. Each NRSA fellow may request $3,000 per budget period to defray childcare costs from a licensed provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Salary Cap, Stipends & Training Funds and What Do Training Funds Pay For? for current stipend levels and allowable costs; include childcare request in budget if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms submission and activation/payback paperwork
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit NRSA forms for activation, payback, and termination via xTrain in eRA Commons or on paper using instructions in Forms Directory—Fellowships and Training. For initial year of NRSA postdoctoral (F32) support, mail activation notice and an original, signed payback agreement to the designated NIAID address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you have an eRA Commons account and follow xTrain training resources; retain original signed payback agreement for mailing when required.
